summary: Your knee MRI on May 14, 2026 was in-network and covered. The allowed amount ($850) goes toward your yearly deductible because you hadn't met it yet. The provider's extra charge ($950) is written off and you don't owe it. You are responsible for the $850 deductible amount.

lines.explanation: This MRI was approved as an in-network service. The plan's allowed amount is $850. Since your deductible was not yet met (you had used $200 of it before this claim), the full $850 allowed amount is applied to your deductible [CODE-PR-1: "PR-1 means this amount was applied to your deductible, the amount you pay each year before the plan starts sharing costs"]. The provider billed $1,800 but agreed to accept $850 as the in-network rate; the extra $950 is written off by the provider [CODE-CO-45: "CO-45 means the provider billed more than the rate they agreed to with the plan. The difference is written off by the provider. Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care"]. You do not owe the $950 writeoff.

actions: Verify that you received prior authorization for this MRI before the service date, as [PLAN-AUTH: "Advanced imaging such as MRI and CT... require prior authorization"].
If you do not have a prior auth confirmation, contact your plan immediately to confirm coverage.
Wait for your deductible to be fully met before the plan begins to share costs on future services.
Do not pay the provider's original $1,800 bill; pay only the $850 in-network allowed amount that counts toward your deductible.
